findings.claim: The design docs still describe the old route. .okf/manifesto.md:64 says APM writes the skills and rules into .agents/ and the plugin folder holds the agents, hook and MCP server, with no rules. .okf/architecture/overview.md:176-201 says the wheel carries only skills/ and agents/ (it now also carries instructions/), the plugin-folder bullet lists no rules/, the rules bullet names only .claude/rules/, and the commands table row (line 160) does not mention deleting kmctl's rules from .agents/rules/. None of them cites ADR 0016.

Row r4's command (-k 'validate or consumer') runs only the agy validate test and test_consumer_gets_skills_rules_and_the_plugin_folder. Neither runs kmctl doctor, so the row's 'doctor exits nonzero' case is not checked by its own command. test_doctor_after_a_real_install_exits_zero covers it, but only under r6 and the integration gate. Assert doctor's exit code in the consumer test, or widen r4's -k to include that test.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan says.
kmctl translates the four instructions into `.agents/plugins/kmctl/rules/` as `trigger: glob` with one comma-separated string of `**/` globs, and the wheel ships `_instructions`.
After APM's install it deletes only the files the lock lists for kmctl's package under `.agents/rules/`, and doctor stops expecting them there.
I can re-check both open findings once they are fixed, and neither blocks: the manifesto and architecture overview still describe the old route (f1), and r4's command does not run doctor (f2).
I ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree myself, with a scratch HOME.
Result: `stamp green: fe5c53a914450a754d0243ab7e543c7684e9e7695e3aadc7cf7f276442318959`.
Lint, format, tests and integration all passed, and r1 to r6 all passed.
The r4 log shows 2 passed with no skip, so agy validate --strict really ran and counted the rules.
The state commit was deferred only because the scratch HOME has no git identity.
I read the full diff of antigravity.py, plugin.py, doctor.py, __init__.py, pyproject.toml, ADR 0016, the ADR 0015 pointer, the index, the log, commands.md, the how-to and the tests.
I ran translate_rule on the four shipped instructions.
The output is `"**/.okf/**, **/src/**, ..."` and similar, single strings with no doubled prefix and the order kept.
Correctness: drop_apm_rules only removes lock-listed paths that start with `.agents/rules/` and are files, so other packages' rules stay.
Antigravity refuses `--scope user` (plugin.py:1014), so `cwd / rel` is the right root.
Reading the lock before the antigravity block is safe because APM has already written it.
When write_plugin raises, nothing is deleted.
Doctor: the `moved` filter applies only to antigravity and to kmctl's package.
In the r3 fixture the lock lists `.agents/rules/okf-bundle.md` and the install deletes it, so the "absent passes" test really exercises the filter.
The missing, edited and extra cases each assert the detail and AG_FIX.
Eval rows.
r1's tests cover a list, a doubled prefix, the order, the body and always_on.
r2's tests cover the translations, the moved test (another file is kept and the skills stay), the wheel and the second install of the plugin folder.
r3 is as above.
r4: see f2.
r5 checks all three pages plus the 0016 pointer in 0015.
Consistency: ADR 0016's rejected options and consequences agree with the code.
The help epilog and the commands.md steps match the code.
See f1 for the design docs.
f1 (docs, non-blocking): .okf/manifesto.md and .okf/architecture/overview.md still say APM supplies Antigravity's rules and that the plugin folder holds only agents, hook and MCP.
They should name rules/ in the plugin folder, the deletion from .agents/rules/, the `_instructions` wheel data and ADR 0016.
f2 (test-strength, non-blocking): r4's command does not run kmctl doctor, so the row's doctor clause is checked only through r6 and the integration gate.
test_adr_audit_fixes now checks `>= 15` instead of `== 15`.
It still catches an empty record list, so this is acceptable.
test_plugin_folder_second_install_changes_nothing compares only the plugin folder, not `.agents/rules/`.
Because the deletion is deterministic, I did not raise this as a finding.
A bare `apm install` puts APM's broken copies back, and doctor's `moved` filter will not flag them.
ADR 0016 records this as a consequence.
A non-mapping front matter, such as a YAML list, gives the "applyTo kmctl cannot read" message.
The wording is slightly off, but no shipped file hits it.
